# Scripts the AI Saves for Itself

A way of getting something that worked once is kept as a reviewed Python file and run later with no AI
(`pkgs/ds/ai/scripts.py`). Decided with the user 2026-11-17. Used today for `from_url`'s browser runs
(`pkgs/ds/ai/extract.py`); the store is meant to hold other kinds later.

## Where

- **Files:** `pkgs/ds/ai/temp/scripts/<id>.py`, committed like any code.
- **`registry.md`** in the same folder: id, description, signature and size per script. **Rebuilt from the
  files** on every save and delete, never edited by hand or by the AI; a test fails when it is out of date.
  The AI is given its rows and reads a file when it needs it.
- **Run history:** `local/ai_scripts/runs.jsonl` (this machine only), so the registry doesn't change per run.

## A script file

- **One public function, named as the file**, every parameter and the return typed, with a docstring: the
  one thing a user would ask for. The file's docstring's first line is its registry description.
- **Everything else is private** (`_parse`, `_url`, `_check`). The models it returns are the only other
  public names.
- **A parameter, not a new script**, for the same site and return shape asked another way (a ticker, a
  range). **Another script** for another site or another return shape. A helper two scripts need stays
  copied until a third needs it.
- **`_url(...)`** (same parameters) says where the page is: what the AI browser falls back to.
  **`_check(result) -> str`** says why a result looks wrong ("" when fine).
- **Rules checked before every save and every run** (`scripts.script_problem`): the top level holds only the
  docstring, allowlisted imports (`json`, `re`, `math`, `datetime`, `typing`, `pydantic`, `page_data`,
  `ds.util.http`), pydantic models, functions and `UPPER_CASE` or `Literal` constants; no `global` /
  `nonlocal`; no `open`, `eval`, `exec`, `getattr`; no private attributes; no assigning to another object's
  attributes; no `from __future__ import annotations`. Open questions are the TODO at the top of
  `registry.md`.

## What must hold

- **Nothing reaches disk unreviewed.** A new script, a repair and a widened script are each shown as code
  first; the user's Enter saves. A saved script is real Python (imports, the browser), unlike the restricted
  parsers of `from_url`, which is why.
- **Verified before it is offered.** A draft is run with no AI and must give (95% of) the rows the AI run
  got; else it goes back to the AI with why, up to three times. Drafts that failed are kept to be shown.
- **Fresh every call.** A run reads the file and executes it in a new namespace: an edit by the user or the
  AI applies on the next call with no restart, nothing of a script stays between calls, and two scripts'
  names can't collide. (Scripts are not imported, so there is nothing to reload or cache.)
- **The user can tell which script was picked.** The `/assign` proposal's code names it and its arguments
  before Enter (`scripts.<id>(...)`), with "a saved script: no AI when run" under it.
- **A script that stops working doesn't stop the user.** It fails when it raises, when its value doesn't fit
  its return type, or when its `_check` refuses the value. Then the AI browser gets the value from the
  script's `_url` (costs a few cents, without asking), the chat says the script failed and why, and
  `/script` offers its repair. If the browser fails too, both reasons show and the script is left as it is.
- **Asked another way, a script is widened, not multiplied.** The draft AI is given the saved scripts for
  the same site with their past calls, and changes one (adds the parameter) instead of writing a second.
- **A size cap asks, it doesn't delete.** Past `MAX_DIR_BYTES` (250,000 bytes of script files), a save still
  happens and the chat lists the scripts, never-run and least recently run first, to delete with
  `/script delete <id>`.
- **`page_data(url, clicks, response)`** is the no-AI browser a script calls: headless system Chromium,
  clicks by visible label, returns the body of the data response whose URL contains `response`. It may not
  reach this machine or a private network, and is logged like any outside request.

## Not done

- A time limit per run; a script calling the AI; shared helper files.
- Showing a repair as a diff (the whole new file is shown).
- "Save as script" for anything but a `from_url` browser run.
